lines.text: Two lines cut this shape into four triangles.
lines.caption: Two lines cut this shape into four triangles.

lines.text: We know the area of just ONE of them. <short pause> Can we find all four?
lines.caption: We know the area of just ONE of them. Can we find all four?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's crack it together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: In trapezoid A B C D, side A B is parallel to side D C.
lines.caption: In trapezoid A B C D, side A B is parallel to side D C.

lines.text: A B is six, and D C is ten.
lines.caption: A B is six, and D C is ten.

lines.text: The diagonals cross at point E. The shaded triangle A B E has area nine.
lines.caption: The diagonals cross at point E. The shaded triangle A B E has area nine.

lines.text: What is the area of the whole trapezoid?
lines.caption: What is the area of the whole trapezoid?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we really know?
lines.caption: So what do we really know?

lines.text: The diagonals split the trapezoid into four triangles: top, bottom, left and right.
lines.caption: The diagonals split the trapezoid into four triangles: top, bottom, left and right.

lines.text: We know the top one is nine. We need all four added up.
lines.caption: We know the top one is nine. We need all four added up.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's look at the top triangle and the bottom triangle.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's look at the top triangle and the bottom triangle.

lines.text: The top and bottom are parallel, so these two angles match. They make a Z shape.
lines.caption: The top and bottom are parallel, so these two angles match. They make a Z shape.

lines.text: These two match as well. That's another Z, along the other diagonal.
lines.caption: These two match as well. That's another Z, along the other diagonal.

lines.text: And the angles at E are opposite each other, so they're equal too.
lines.caption: And the angles at E are opposite each other, so they're equal too.

lines.text: Same angles make the same shape! The bottom triangle is a blown-up copy of the top one.
lines.caption: Same angles make the same shape! The bottom triangle is a blown-up copy of the top one.

lines.text: How much bigger? The top side is six, the bottom side is ten.
lines.caption: How much bigger? The top side is six, the bottom side is ten.

lines.text: Six to ten is the same as three to five. So every length grows by five over three.
lines.caption: Six to ten is the same as three to five. So every length grows by five over three.

lines.text: Now here's the key step. What happens to the area?
lines.caption: Now here's the key step. What happens to the area?

lines.text: The base grows by five over three. And the height grows by five over three too.
lines.caption: The base grows by five over three. And the height grows by five over three too.

lines.text: So the area grows by five over three, TWICE. That's twenty-five over nine.
lines.caption: So the area grows by five over three, TWICE. That's twenty-five over nine.

lines.text: Nine times twenty-five over nine is twenty-five. The bottom triangle is twenty-five!
lines.caption: Nine times twenty-five over nine is twenty-five. The bottom triangle is twenty-five!

lines.text: Now the triangle on the right, B C E. Look at it next to the top triangle.
lines.caption: Now the triangle on the right, B C E. Look at it next to the top triangle.

lines.text: They share the corner B, and their bases sit on the same diagonal.
lines.caption: They share the corner B, and their bases sit on the same diagonal.

lines.text: So they have the same height! Their areas compare just like their bases.
lines.caption: So they have the same height! Their areas compare just like their bases.

lines.text: In our copy, A E matches C E. So A E to E C is three to five.
lines.caption: In our copy, A E matches C E. So A E to E C is three to five.

lines.text: So the triangle on the right is nine times five over three. That's fifteen.
lines.caption: So the triangle on the right is nine times five over three. That's fifteen.

lines.text: The triangle on the left works the same way, using the other diagonal. It's fifteen too.
lines.caption: The triangle on the left works the same way, using the other diagonal. It's fifteen too.

lines.text: Let's add them all up. Nine, plus twenty-five, plus fifteen, plus fifteen.
lines.caption: Let's add them all up. Nine, plus twenty-five, plus fifteen, plus fifteen.

lines.text: That's sixty-four! The answer is D.
lines.caption: That's sixty-four! The answer is D.

lines.text: Here's a second way. The top triangle has base six and area nine.
lines.caption: Here's a second way. The top triangle has base six and area nine.

lines.text: Half of six, times its height, is nine. So its height is three.
lines.caption: Half of six, times its height, is nine. So its height is three.

lines.text: The bottom triangle is the five over three copy. So its height is three times five over three. That's five.
lines.caption: The bottom triangle is the five over three copy. So its height is three times five over three. That's five.

lines.text: Stack them up. The whole trapezoid is three plus five, which is eight, tall.
lines.caption: Stack them up. The whole trapezoid is three plus five, which is eight, tall.

lines.text: Trapezoid area: add the top and bottom, take half, then times the height.
lines.caption: Trapezoid area: add the top and bottom, take half, then times the height.

lines.text: Six plus ten is sixteen. Half is eight. Eight times eight is sixty-four!
lines.caption: Six plus ten is sixteen. Half is eight. Eight times eight is sixty-four!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? It's fast, and it's a great double-check.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? It's fast, and it's a great double-check.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Thirty-four is just the top and bottom triangles. It forgets the two side ones.
lines.caption: Thirty-four is just the top and bottom triangles. It forgets the two side ones.

lines.text: Forty-nine counts only one side triangle, not both.
lines.caption: Forty-nine counts only one side triangle, not both.

lines.text: Fifty-four is what you'd get if you grew the area by five over three only once.
lines.caption: Fifty-four is what you'd get if you grew the area by five over three only once.

lines.text: Sixty-eight is what you'd get if each side triangle were halfway between nine and twenty-five.
lines.caption: Sixty-eight is what you'd get if each side triangle were halfway between nine and twenty-five.

lines.text: Halfway is seventeen. But the true side area is nine times five over three, which is fifteen.
lines.caption: Halfway is seventeen. But the true side area is nine times five over three, which is fifteen.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Always count every piece, and square the scale for areas.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Always count every piece, and square the scale for areas.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new trapezoid.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new trapezoid.

lines.text: The top is four, and the bottom is eight.
lines.caption: The top is four, and the bottom is eight.

lines.text: The top triangle has area four. What is the area of the whole trapezoid?
lines.caption: The top triangle has area four. What is the area of the whole trapezoid?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Four to eight is one to two. So the bottom is a copy, twice as big.
lines.caption: Let's check. Four to eight is one to two. So the bottom is a copy, twice as big.

lines.text: Area grows by two, twice. That's four. So the bottom triangle is four times four, which is sixteen.
lines.caption: Area grows by two, twice. That's four. So the bottom triangle is four times four, which is sixteen.

lines.text: Each side triangle is four times two. That's eight.
lines.caption: Each side triangle is four times two. That's eight.

lines.text: Four, plus sixteen, plus eight, plus eight. That's thirty-six!
lines.caption: Four, plus sixteen, plus eight, plus eight. That's thirty-six!

lines.text: Check with heights. Half of four, times the height, is four. So the top height is two.
lines.caption: Check with heights. Half of four, times the height, is four. So the top height is two.

lines.text: The bottom height is twice that, four. Two plus four is six.
lines.caption: The bottom height is twice that, four. Two plus four is six.

lines.text: Four plus eight is twelve. Half is six. Six times six is thirty-six. It matches!
lines.caption: Four plus eight is twelve. Half is six. Six times six is thirty-six. It matches!

lines.text: If you found thirty-six, amazing work!
lines.caption: If you found thirty-six, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: The diagonals cut a trapezoid into four triangles. The top and bottom ones are copies.
lines.caption: The diagonals cut a trapezoid into four triangles. The top and bottom ones are copies.

lines.text: Lengths grow by the scale. Areas grow by the scale, twice.
lines.caption: Lengths grow by the scale. Areas grow by the scale, twice.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
